# Nadir

> Nadir is a 2D top-down game engine for desktop, written in Rust from the ground up by Joseph Abbott III, with no third-party crates: its own OS bindings, OpenGL renderer, ECS, collision, codecs and tools. https://jabbott.dev/Nadir/ plays the engine's sandbox game as commit {{commit_short}} draws it, recorded in CI, and lists the engine's features with how far each has come.

Key facts:

- Status: in development, {{tasks_done}} of {{tasks_total}} roadmap tasks done at commit {{commit_short}} of {{commit_date}} ({{commit_subject}})
- Language: Rust {{toolchain}}, edition 2024; {{crates}} crates in the workspace; third-party crates: {{third_party}}
- Targets: Windows 10+ and Linux (X11) on x86_64 and aarch64, and macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon and Intel). Only Linux draws so far: the Windows and macOS windows (roadmap M1.5, M1.6, still to be checked by hand) stay empty until their OpenGL contexts land (M2.6, M2.7).
- Out of scope: web and WASM, Android, iOS, consoles, 3D and networking
- License: Apache-2.0
- Source: {{repository_url}}
- Author: Joseph Abbott III, software engineer (https://jabbott.dev/resume/)
